subject: RE: Performance questionnaire and runbook for peak surge acceptance
messages:
From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@novacorp.com>

Cc: NovaCorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance questionnaire — peak surge scenarios

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for taking our RFP. Procurement sent over the performance section and asked for an explicit testing runbook covering:
- Representative request mixes for our peak campaigns (chat + structured generation + embeddings)
- 99th/99.9th percentile latency expectations under steady-state and 10x surge for 30 minutes
- Cold-start behavior (first token latencies after idle) and warmup guidance
- Guidance on congestion behaviors and fallback model variants

We'd like a single consolidated response we can attach to our procurement file. Also, can you include any reproducible test harness config (load profiles, seed prompts) you recommend?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement wants the doc by end of week.

Regards,
Alex Jones
Senior Sourcing Analyst
NovaCorp

P.S. copying procurement so their team has visibility.

From: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@novacorp.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, NovaCorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Performance questionnaire — peak surge scenarios

Hi Alex —

Thanks — we put together a focused package that addresses each bullet and includes reproducible artifacts. Key highlights up front:

- Test approach: workload-driven, hybrid synthetic + sampled production traces. We provide a load harness (YAML) that drives a mix of chat (50%), structured generation/complete (30%), and embedding calls (20%) with adjustable concurrency and sequence-length distributions.
- Latency targets: for the model family you referenced in the RFP, typical steady-state p99 is ~220ms token-level (single-turn median per first response) at 250 qps per GPU; p99.9 measured at 420ms under controlled lab runs. Under a 10x sustained burst (30 minutes) with proper autoscaling configured, p99 shifts to ~600ms; without autoscaling and with capacity saturation, tails can grow non-linearly — we document degradation modes and recommended throttles.
- Cold-starts: cold-start (idle to first request) depends on model variant and hosting mode. In Hosted mode cold-starts for a pinned model with no active KV cache are typically 1.2–1.8s for full docker/container initialization; warming strategies (pre-warm pools, keepalive) reduce this to sub-200ms for subsequent requests.
- Fallbacks: we recommend a 3-tier fallback policy (primary -> quantized variant -> small-latency model) with conservative sequence-length thresholds to preserve correctness while protecting tail latency.

I've attached: redwood_peak_surge_casebook.pdf (narrative + graphs), runbook_test_harness_config.yaml (executable harness), latency_samples_202605.csv (raw sample outputs).

We can provide additional run results if you share the specific model variant, expected request size distribution, and target SLA you need in the contract.

Next steps: if procurement is OK, we can schedule a 30-minute lab-walkthrough with your SREs and spin up a targeted run against a representative request set.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Sales — Performance & Solutions
Redwood Inference

--

Attachment: runbook_test_harness_config.yaml (text)

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Performance questionnaire — small technical clarifications

Alex / team —

Quick addendum from runtime: a few technical clarifications that affect measured tail behavior and should be called out in your acceptance criteria:

1) Kernel selection & quantization: different quantized kernels produce different latency distributions. When we say "quantized variant" in the casebook we mean INT8 kernels tuned for the target GPU family. Please specify whether you require equivalence checks (logprob deltas) for quantized variants — that impacts allowed fallback policies.

2) Batching regime: our runtime uses continuous batching; effective latency depends heavily on QPS granularity and request size distribution. We include a recommended batching policy in the YAML with example batch-timeouts (8ms) and max-batch-size per GPU. If you're benchmarking, please run with the provided harness settings so results are reproducible.

3) Warmup sequences: we recommend a warmup deck that mirrors 20% of your long-tail prompts (top 5k unique prompts) for the 3 hours prior to acceptance testing to saturate KV caches. The runbook includes a warmup script.

Happy to jump on the walkthrough and go line-by-line if needed.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Principal Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Aisha / Aditya —

Thanks for the materials. A couple follow-ups procurement asked us to clarify before we include the doc in the SOW:
- Can you provide p99.99 numbers for the steady-state runs (our SLA language calls for 99.99 in narrow windows)?
- Do you have trace-level examples for requests that triggered fallback (we want to review how output fidelity deviated on fallbacks)?
- For cold-starts, is the 1.2–1.8s number inclusive of model download/asset staging for Private on-prem installs or only Hosted?

If you can drop answers in-line and we can get an amended PDF, that would close procurement's checklist. Also confirm whether the included CSV is raw samples or aggregated buckets.

Appreciate the timely response — we are trying to move the contract into legal next week.

Best,
Alex

From: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@novacorp.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, NovaCorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Performance questionnaire — final clarifications and artifacts

Alex —

See inline answers and attached updated casebook (redwood_peak_surge_casebook_v2.pdf). Quick summary:

- p99.99: steady-state lab runs for the referenced model show p99.99 in the 780–1,050ms range depending on sequence length distribution; those numbers assume no pre-warming and single-region capacity. We call this out because p99.99 is highly sensitive to microbursts and autoscaling cadence.

- Fallback traces: attached is a short trace sample (fallback_traces.txt) with three representative cases and the measured token-level divergence vs primary model. We include a short rubric describing acceptable logprob delta thresholds for your engineering review.

- Cold-starts: the 1.2–1.8s figure I quoted earlier is for Hosted mode where container startup and model warming are measured end-to-end. For Private (on-prem) installs, cold-start is dominated by asset staging: if images and model files are pre-baked on nodes, numbers align with Hosted; if model artifacts must be pulled from a central artifact store during the window, add an additional ~800ms–2.5s depending on network/storage. We recommend pre-staging artifacts as part of any acceptance test.

- CSV provenance: latency_samples_202605.csv is raw per-request samples (timestamp, request-type, seq-len, latency-ms, backend-queue-ms). We included an aggregated summary in the v2 PDF.

Attachments included in this message: redwood_peak_surge_casebook_v2.pdf, fallback_traces.txt, runbook_test_harness_config.yaml (same as prior), latency_samples_202605.csv.

If procurement is satisfied we can lock these artifacts into the SOW and schedule the 30-minute walkthrough with my team and Aditya next week. Evelyn from our Solutions Engineering team is copied for scheduling and acceptance-criteria alignment.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Sales — Performance & Solutions
Redwood Inference
